2216.subject: Zoology
2216.text: Two opposite forces operate in the growth and development of every population. One of them is related to the ability to reproduce at a given rate. The force opposite to it is called
2216.sol: The environmental factors which can check the growth of population size constitute the environmental resistance. These include predators, food, water, nesting sites, similar competitors, etc. All living things tend to reproduce until the point at which their environment becomes a limiting factor. No population, human or otherwise, can grow indefinitely; eventually, some biotic or abiotic variable will begin to limit population growth.

2221.subject: Zoology
2221.text: Keystone species deserve protection because these
options: are capable of surviving in harsh environmental conditions
indicate presence of certain minerals in the soil
have become rare due to overexploitation
play an important role in supporting other species.
2221.sol: Keystone species is a species which has significant and disproportionately large influence on the community removal or decrease in number of keystone species causes disruption in structure and function of community. For example in intertidal regions star fish feeds on mussels. Removal of star fish leads to dominance of mussels that excludes algae and browsing species. In tropical rain forests fig functions as keystone species as they provide fruit to a number of animals during the period of food scarcity.

Compounds of Cr(VI) such as CrO ₃ , CrO ₄²⁻ , and Cr ₂ O ₇²⁻ are strong oxidising agents because Cr(VI) can easily be reduced to the more stable Cr(III) state. 70965.subject: Biology
70965.text: Which enzyme in the midgut of insect is instrumental in the release of core toxic fragments from bacterial spores ingested by it?
70965.sol: Bacillus thuringiensis produces proteinaceous toxins in an inactive form called protoxins. When an insect ingests these spores or crystals, the alkaline pH of the insect's midgut solubilizes the crystals. Subsequently, midgut proteinases (proteases) cleave the inactive protoxin into its active core toxic fragments. These active toxins bind to the surface of midgut epithelial cells, creating pores that cause cell swelling and lysis, eventually leading to the death of the insect. Answer: Proteinase

71985.text: The maximum amount of a solid solute that can be dissolved in a specified amount of a given liquid solvent does NOT depend upon
71985.sol: The solubility of a solid in a liquid depends on the nature of the solute, the nature of the solvent, and the temperature. Since solids and liquids are highly incompressible, pressure has practically no significant effect on the solubility of a solid in a liquid. Answer: Pressure

75296.subject: General Ability
75296.text: In the soil-forming regime, which one of the following occurs in a region where evapotranspiration exceeds precipitation significantly?
75296.sol: Calcification occurs when evapotranspiration exceeds precipitation causing the upward movement of dissolved alkaline salts from the groundwater. At the same time, the movement of rain water causes a downward movement of the salts. The net result is the deposition of the translocated cations in the B horizon. Calcification is common in the prairie grasslands.

79243.subject: Mathematics
79243.text: ABC is a triangle right-angled at B . If A(k, 1, -1) , B(2k, 0, 2) and C(2+2k, k, 1) are the vertices of the triangle, then what is the value of k ?
79243.sol: The direction ratios of the line segment AB are (k - 2k, 1 - 0, -1 - 2) = (-k, 1, -3) . The direction ratios of the line segment BC are (2+2k - 2k, k - 0, 1 - 2) = (2, k, -1) . Since the triangle is right-angled at B , the line segments AB and BC are perpendicular to each other. Therefore, the dot product of their direction ratios is zero. 80214.subject: Botany
80214.text: Kranz anatomy is one of the characteristics of the leaves of
80214.sol: Sugarcane is a C ₄ -plant. C ₄ -plants are characterised by the presence of ' Kranz ^ (German term meaning halo or wreath) type of anatomy. In this, the leaf mesophyll is undifferentiated and its cells (having normal type of granal chloroplasts) occur in concentric layers around vascular bundles, later is surrounded by large-sized bundle sheath cells (having large-sized agranal chloroplasts) which are arranged in a wreath like manner.

80562.subject: Botany
80562.text: What is the function of germ pore?
options: Absorption of water for seed germination
80562.sol: The pollen grain has two layers-outer exine and inner intine. Exine is made up of highly resistant sporopollenin while intine is pectocellulosic. At certain places exine is thin or absent called germpore or germinal furrow. After reaching on stigma the pollen grain absorbs water and nutrients from the stigmatic secretion through its germ pore. The tube or vegetative cell enlarges. It comes out of the pollen grain through one of the germ pores or germinal furrows to form a pollen tube.

80628.subject: Botany
80628.text: Movement and accumulation of ions across a membrane against their concentration gradient can be explained by:
80628.sol: One of the main way of transport of solute or molecules in plant cells is called active transport. Active transport uses energy to transport and pump molecules against a concentration gradient. This is carried out by specific membrane-bound proteins or pumps. These protein pumps use energy (derived from ATP) to carry substances across the cell membrane. These pumps can transport substances from a low concentration to a high concentration (‘uphill’ transport).

options: Movement of air into and out of the lungs
Pressure gradient between the lungs and the atmosphere
Negative pressure in the lungs with respect to atmospheric pressure
Intra-pulmonary pressure higher than atmospheric pressure
129810.sol: Breathing involves two stages : inspiration during which atmospheric air is drawn in and expiration by which the alveolar air is released out. The movement of air into and out of the lungs is carried out by creating a pressure gradient between the lungs and the atmosphere. Inspiration can occur if the pressure within the lungs (intra-pulmonary pressure) is less than the atmospheric pressure, i.e., there is a negative pressure in the lungs with respect to atmospheric pressure. 130234.subject: Zoology
130234.text: What are the two principal divisions of the Skeletal system?
130234.sol: The Skeletal system is grouped into two main divisions - the axial skeleton which includes the bones that make up the central axis of the body such as the skull, spinal column, rib cage and the appendicular skeleton which includes bones of the upper and lower limbs and the bones that attach the limbs to the axial skeleton. Bones play a crucial role in supporting and providing structure to the human body. They also protect delicate organs, store minerals, and produce blood cells.

The enlarged end of penis called the glans penis is covered by a loose fold of skin called foreskin. The male accessory glands include paired seminal vesicles, a prostate and paired bulbourethral glands. 130852.text: are the female accessory ducts in the reproductive system?
130852.sol: The oviducts (fallopian tubes), uterus and vagina constitute the female accessory ducts. Each fallopian tube is about 10-12 cm long and extends from the periphery of each ovary to the uterus, the part closer to the ovary is the funnel-shaped infundibulum. The edges of the infundibulum possess finger-like projections called fimbriae, which help in collection of the ovum after ovulation. 132032.subject: Zoology
132032.text: When did humans know that one of the causes of variation was hidden in sexual reproduction?
132032.sol: Explanation : Humans knew from as early as 8000-1000 B.C. that one of the causes of variation was hidden in sexual reproduction. They exploited the variations that were naturally present in the wild populations of plants and animals to selectively breed and select for organisms that possessed desirable characters. For example, through artificial selection and domestication from ancestral wild cows, we have well-known Indian breeds, e.g., Sahiwal cows in Punjab. 132179.subject: Zoology
132179.text: What was one of the main reasons Mendel's concept of genes was not accepted by his contemporaries?
options: His idea of discrete units controlling traits was new
His theories were published too late
132179.sol: Mendel published his work on inheritance of characters in 1865 but for several reasons, it remained unrecognized till 1900. Firstly, communication was not easy (as it is now) in those days and his work could not be widely publicized. 132420.subject: Zoology
132420.text: Which of the following traits or disorders in humans is a classic example of polygenic inheritance?
132420.sol: Polygenic inheritance refers to traits that are controlled by three or more genes. In humans, skin colour and height are classic examples of polygenic inheritance. Phenylketonuria is an example of pleiotropy, where a single gene mutation causes multiple phenotypic effects. Sickle cell anaemia and haemophilia are Mendelian disorders caused by mutation in a single gene. Answer: Human skin colour

132436.subject: Zoology
132436.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding sickle cell anaemia. List-I List-II (A) Affected globin chain (I) Autosomal recessive (B) Amino acid substitution (II) Beta chain (C) mRNA codon for mutant allele (III) GUG (D) Inheritance pattern (IV) Glutamic acid to Valine Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
132436.sol: Sickle cell anaemia is an autosomal recessive trait (D-I). It is caused by a point mutation that affects the beta globin chain of the haemoglobin molecule (A-II). The mutation results in the substitution of Glutamic acid by Valine at the sixth position of the beta globin chain (B-IV). This amino acid substitution is due to a single base substitution at the sixth codon of the beta globin gene, changing the mRNA codon from GAG to GUG (C-III). Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(III), (D)-(I).

6a13e465688ac6d0667aacfc.subject: Physics
6a13e465688ac6d0667aacfc.text: The work done in stretching a linear spring by 4 cm from its natural length is 10 J . The additional work required to stretch it further by another 8 cm will be:
6a13e465688ac6d0667aacfc.sol: The work done in stretching a spring by a distance x from its natural length is given by W = 1 2 kx^2 . Given W₁ = 10 J for x₁ = 4 cm . W₁ = 1 2 k(4)^2 = 10 The final extension of the spring is x₂ = 4 cm + 8 cm = 12 cm . The total work done to stretch the spring by 12 cm is W₂ = 1 2 k(12)^2 . Taking the ratio of W₂ to W₁ : W₂ W₁ = ( 12 4 )^2 = 3^2 = 9 W₂ = 9 10 = 90 J The additional work required is W = W₂ - W₁ = 90 J - 10 J = 80 J . Answer: 80 J

95921.text: Term genome/nucleoid can be used for:
95921.sol: In prokaryotic cells, the nucleus is in primitive form. In this nucleus nuclear membrane and histone proteins are absent, so the nucleus is present in scattered form. This nucleus is called the incipient nucleus/nucleoid/genophore. Bacteria, mycoplasma, archaebacteria, and cyanobacteria (Blue-green algae) all are prokaryotes with primitive nucleus.

96074.subject: Botany
96074.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding mitochondria?
options: The matrix possesses a single double-stranded circular DNA molecule.
It is the site of anaerobic respiration.
The outer membrane is continuous and smooth.
Mitochondria multiply by a fission-like division.
96074.sol: Mitochondria is the site for aerobic respiration. It is surrounded by two membranes, the outer membrane which is smooth, and the inner membrane which is folded into finger-like projections called cristae. Mitochondria divide by fission to increases its number.

96160.subject: Botany
96160.text: Some cells in the adult animals do not appear to exhibit division (e.g., heart cells) and many other cells divide only occasionally. Such cells are said to be in
96160.sol: Some cells in the adult animals do not appear to exhibit division (e.g., heart cells) and many other cells divide only occasionally, as needed to replace cells that have been lost because of injury or cell death. These cells do not divide further exit G 1 phase to enter an inactive stage called quiescent stage (G 0 ) of the cell cycle. Cells in this stage remain metabolically active but no longer proliferate unless called on to do so depending on the requirement of the organism.

96241.subject: Botany
96241.text: Meiosis is one of the two cell division process observed to occur in cells. Which statement from below correctly describes the outcome of a successful meiotic division?
options: Four daughter cells are produced. Each resulting daughter cell has the same number of chromosomes as the paren
Two daughter cells are produced Each resulting daughter cell has the same number of chromosomes as the parent
Four daughter cells are produced. Each resulting daughter cell has one-half the number of chromosomes as the p
Two daughter cells are produced. Each resulting daughter cell has one-half the number of chromosomes as the pa
96241.sol: Meiotic division is a type of cell division where two cell division occurs with only one round of DNA duplication process. The eventual new cells that are formed have half the genetic content of the participating cells. If a participating cell has 20 chromosome, its eventual daughter cell will have 10 chromosome. Thus, the statement of each daughter cell having one-half the number of chromosomes as the parent cell is the correct one. Mitosis is another type of cell division process where the DNA duplication occurs

96541.subject: Botany
96541.text: If we completely remove the decomposers from an ecosystem, the ecosystem functioning will be adversely affected because:
options: Herbivores will not receive solar energy
Rate of deposition of other component will be very high.
96541.sol: Heterotrophic organisms like bacteria and fungi act as decomposers which degrade the dead organic matter or detritus which in turn provides energy and nutrition. Decomposers secrete gastric enzymes resulting in the breakdown of dead organic matter into simple inorganic substances which are then absorbed in the soil and used by producers to grow. Hence if the decomposers are removed from the ecosystem, nutrients will not be available to producers which block the flow of minerals from producers to consumers.

Equal distribution of auxin in the stem.
Equal distribution of a neurotransmitter in the stem.
97272.sol: The plant hormone, auxin, is more distributed on the side away from the unilateral illumination causing cells to grow faster in the darker side, which in turn, causes the plant to bend toward the light. If the distribution were equal, the plant would grow just upwards. Neuro-transmitters are chemicals secreted by multicellular animals and are used in transmitting impulses in the nervous system.

97766.subject: Botany
97766.sol: Respiration is part of the metabolic process where the nutrients are converted into useful energy for regular cell activities. It is in two-mode depending on the presence or absence of oxygen. Aerobic respiration is the one where oxygen is involved and anaerobic respiration is the process where oxygen is absent. Respiration is generally considered catabolic as the complex compounds are broken into simpler forms to produce energy. Although, respiration has been found to be both catabolic and anabolic. 98270.subject: Chemistry
98270.text: An enzyme catalyses a reaction by _________ activation energy of the reaction.
98270.sol: Enzyme catalyses a reaction by lowering down the activation energy of the reaction so that the reaction can occur at normal cellular condition. Activation energy is lowered by using binding energy which is released when substrate binds to active site of enzyme to form ES complex. Thus ES complex formation is very much necessary for enzyme catalysed reaction to occur.

Secondary metabolites are waste product or excretory products which are converted to non toxic forms, these are present in plants, bacteria and fungi.

304886.text: Consider a frame of reference that is fixed to the earth. Which of the following statements are correct regarding this frame?
options: It is defined as an inertial frame by default.
It cannot be an inertial frame since the earth revolves around the sun.
It cannot be an inertial frame since the earth rotates about its axis.
It qualifies as an inertial frame because Newton's laws are valid within it.
304886.sol: A frame of reference fixed to the earth is a non-inertial frame because the earth is an accelerating body. The earth rotates about its own axis, which provides a centripetal acceleration to any point on its surface. The earth also revolves around the sun, which involves a centripetal acceleration directed towards the sun. Since the frame is accelerating, it is non-inertial.

304811.chapter: Wave Motion and Waves on a String
304811.text: A longitudinal wave is unable to
304811.sol: Polarization is a phenomenon restricted to transverse waves, where the direction of oscillation is perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation. In longitudinal waves, the particles of the medium oscillate along the direction of wave propagation. Since there is only one axis of oscillation, longitudinal waves cannot be polarized. Like all waves, longitudinal waves transfer energy and can possess a unique wave velocity and wavelength.

306766.text: Suppose a charged particle is projected inside a gravity-free room and experiences a deflection. Which of the following statements apply?
options: the two fields cannot both be zero
a magnetic field is necessarily present
an electric field is necessarily present
the two fields can both be nonzero
306766.sol: The force on a moving charge q with velocity v in an electric field E and magnetic field B is given by the Lorentz force: F = q( E + v B ) For the particle to experience a deflection, the net force perpendicular to its velocity must be non-zero. If both E and B are zero, the net force is zero, and the particle will move in a straight line without any deflection. Hence, the two fields cannot both be zero. 306731.sol: The displacement current between the plates of a capacitor is given by I_d = ₀ d _E dt The electric flux between the plates is _E = E A = ( q ₀ A ) A = q ₀ Substituting this into the expression for displacement current, we get: I_d = ₀ d dt ( q ₀ ) = dq dt This shows that the displacement current is non-zero whenever the charge q on the capacitor changes with time. 306706.subject: Physics
306706.text: As a result of the space charge in a diode valve,
options: the emission rate of thermions increases
306706.sol: In a diode valve, the space charge is the accumulation of emitted electrons in the region between the cathode and the anode. Since electrons are negatively charged, this electron cloud exerts a repulsive force on the newly emitted thermions from the cathode. Due to this repulsion, some of the emitted electrons are pushed back towards the cathode and are unable to reach the anode. Consequently, the net flow of electrons to the plate is reduced, which means the plate current decreases.
